questions.question_text:
A student's working for $6-3(x+1)=9$ is shown.
$6-3(x+1)=9$
$6-3x+3=9$
$9-3x=9$
$x=0$
The student made one mistake.
What is the correct solution?

options.why: Repeats the student's error of expanding $-3(x+1)$ as $-3x+3$ instead of $-3x-3$.
Expanded correctly to $-3x=6$ but divided without keeping the negative sign.
Added $3$ to the right side instead of subtracting it, giving $-3x=12$.

questions.solution_text:
The $-3$ must multiply both terms in the bracket, so $-3(x+1)=-3x-3$.
$6-3(x+1)=9$
$6-3x-3=9$
$3-3x=9$
$-3x=6$
$x=-2$
